# SDK Generator

> Published task guides for SDK Generator.


## Go SDK Generator: task guides

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


`go-sdk-generator` turns a validated YAML or JSON operation contract into a Go SDK, an optional CLI, and supporting project files. Use these guides to move from a manifest to a working project. The [generated command reference](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DOCUMENTATION.md) lists every CLI option; the guides explain when and how to use them.

### Choose a task

- [Install and inspect the tool](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/install-and-inspect.html): choose a package or OCI image, check the CLI, and inspect the schema.
- [Write a manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html): define a focused project, choose types and constraints, and validate the contract.
- [What the generator produces](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/what-it-generates.html): SDK, CLI, action and documentation outputs, and what remains to implement.
- [Types, formats and defaults](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/types-and-defaults.html): choose built-in `lang_type` values and generated default behaviour.
- [Configure functional options](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/configure-options.html): enable option values and expose them through CLI flags.
- [Generate and regenerate a project](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/generate-a-project.html): run generation, implement operations, and preserve handwritten work.
- [Use the GitHub Actions](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/use-github-actions.html): run generation in a workflow or install the binary for later steps.
- [Manage secrets in a generated CLI](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/secret-management.html): mark secret inputs, use keyring-backed commands and understand security boundaries.
- [Evolve a contract safely](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/evolving-a-contract.html): deprecate incompatible manifest and generated-surface changes.

### Further reference

- [Schema source](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml): authoritative manifest field definitions.
- [This repository's manifest](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generate.yml): a real generator input.
- [Generated SDK and CLI reference](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DOCUMENTATION.md): configuration, commands, and Go interfaces.
- [Repository README](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/README.md): purpose, quick start and design decisions.
- [Maintained agent skills](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/tree/main/.agents/skills): task-specific instructions for agents working in this repository. The tool can also install its embedded skills with `go-sdk-generator agent --init`.

The Markdown in `guides/` is the source. `cd-generate-docs` renders it alongside the API documentation in `docs/guides/` when documentation is rebuilt; edit the Markdown rather than the rendered output.


## Configure functional options

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


Use `specification.options` in a [generator manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html) to define optional settings for an SDK operation and, where needed, expose them in the generated CLI. The [repository's pet shop manifest](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/testdata/petshop-purchase.yml) exercises the option and CLI configuration together.

### Define an option and its value field

Each generated option value has an `Enabled bool` field with `mapstructure:"enabled"`. A `default_value` prepares its value but does **not** enable the option. Calling a generated `With…(...)` helper enables it, even if the supplied value is empty. The `value_field` setting changes the name and mapstructure tag of the value held by the option; it does not rename the enabling flag.

For example, within `specification`:

```yaml
options:
  - name: Search
    package: search
    description: Functional options for product catalogue searches.
    functions:
      - parameters:
          - name: PageToken
            lang_type: string
            description: Continuation token for the next page.
            value_field:
              name: Token
              mapstructure_tag: token
```

This defines a wrapper with a separate enabling state:

```go
type SearchOptionsPageTokenOption struct {
    Token   string `mapstructure:"token"`
    Enabled bool   `mapstructure:"enabled"`
}
```

Without `value_field`, the value is named `PageToken` with a `page_token` mapstructure tag. With `name: Token`, `mapstructure_tag` is optional and also defaults to `token`.

**Migration:** Option parameters no longer accept `bindings`. Replace an option-level `bindings: [{name: Token, mapstructure_tag: token}]` with `value_field: {name: Token, mapstructure_tag: token}`. CLI configuration `bindings` still control flags and environment mappings. For other incompatible changes, see [breaking changes and deprecation](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/evolving-a-contract.html).

### Expose the option in a CLI command

Use the generated wrapper as a command configuration field. For example, within `specification.command_line_commands.functions[].configuration`:

```yaml
- name: PageTokenOption
  lang_type: search.SearchOptionsPageTokenOption
  mapstructure_tag: page_token
  description: Use a continuation token for the catalogue search.
  bindings:
    - name: Token
      lang_type: string
      mapstructure_tag: token
      arg: page-token-value
      description: Continuation token value.
```

The generated CLI binds `--page-token-value` to the option's `Token` value. It also creates `--page-token` to set `Enabled`, with an environment binding for `PAGE_TOKEN_ENABLED` under the command's environment prefix. The generated default configuration retains the option's default value, if any, with `Enabled: false`.

You can rename the enabling CLI flag by adding an `Enabled` binding to the **CLI configuration field**, not the option parameter:

```yaml
- name: PageSizeOption
  lang_type: search.SearchOptionsPageSizeOption
  mapstructure_tag: page_size
  description: Apply the configured page size.
  bindings:
    - name: Enabled
      lang_type: bool
      mapstructure_tag: enabled
      arg: use-paging
      description: Enable paging.
```

This changes the default `--page-size` flag to `--use-paging` while retaining the `PageSizeOption.Enabled` destination and its environment binding. Omit the binding to keep the default flag name. See the [pet shop manifest](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/testdata/petshop-purchase.yml) for the complete option and CLI definitions.


## Breaking changes and deprecation

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


Use this guide when changing an existing [generator manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html) or a generated SDK, CLI or automation surface that consumers already use. The aim is to make contract evolution reviewable and migratable.

### Identify a breaking change

A change is breaking when existing manifest authors or generated-project consumers must edit a working configuration, integration or workflow. Examples include:

- renaming or removing a field, method, command, parameter or type;
- changing the meaning of an existing field incompatibly;
- tightening validation so previously valid manifests become invalid;
- changing a value shape from scalar to list, value to reference, or one incompatible type to another;
- replacing one concept with several new ones, or merging several existing concepts into one.

### Deprecate before removing

A deprecation is a transition: the old concept still works but points users to its replacement. Where practical:

1. Add the replacement first.
2. Mark the old concept with `deprecation_notice` in the manifest.
3. Name the replacement and state when deprecation begins and, when known, when removal is planned.
4. Surface the notice in generated documentation, comments and CLI help.
5. Keep the deprecated behaviour working during the transition unless safety or correctness requires otherwise.
6. Remove it only after the announced window and a migration opportunity.

### Versioning and news files

This repository follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) conceptually: breaking changes are major in theory, features minor and fixes patch. A true `v2+` release of a Go project also changes its module and consumer import paths; it is not merely a version-number bump ([Go modules](https://go.dev/ref/mod#major-version-suffix), [Go Modules: v2 and beyond](https://go.dev/blog/v2-go-modules)).

Do not treat every breaking manifest change as an automatic major-module migration. If a change breaks consumers without a full Go major-module transition, describe the break explicitly in a `.feature` news file, for example with a `:boom:` prefix. Reserve `.major` news files for a genuine major Go module migration, including its import-path consequences. See the [contribution guide](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#news-files) for news-file conventions.

In short: **deprecate, document, migrate, then remove**. For detailed authoring checks, use the [manifest-authoring skill](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/.agents/skills/manifest-authoring/SKILL.md).


## Generate and regenerate a Go project

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


### Inputs and first run

You need a manifest that follows the [schema](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml), an output directory, and a target Go version matching the project. From the project directory:

```sh
go-sdk-generator generate -i generate.yml -o . --go-version 1.27.3
```

Replace the Go version with the version your project uses. `-i`/`--input` selects the manifest, `-o`/`--output` selects the destination, and `-g`/`--go-version` selects the target Go version. Use `go-sdk-generator generate --help` for current options. The generator validates the manifest before producing files.

After generation, run these commands from each directory containing a generated `go.mod`:

```sh
go mod tidy
go generate ./...
go test ./...
```

`go mod tidy` resolves dependencies; `go generate ./...` runs generated directives, such as mock generation. Implement the generated operation stubs in Go and test the resulting behaviour. The manifest is the source of truth for the *surface*, not an implementation of the operations.

Also review generated repository automation files such as `pyproject.toml` and `.github/workflows/`. Top-level manifest settings like `tag_latest` and `update_copyright_headers` change those outputs. On an existing project, use `--overwrite` to update stateful generated files such as `pyproject.toml` and the workflows. If you turn off automatic copyright maintenance, remove any previously generated licensing workflow that remains in the project.

For a multi-module workspace, repeat the commands in each generated module rather than running `go mod tidy` from the workspace root. See [what the generator produces](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/what-it-generates.html) for the distinction between generated scaffolding and handwritten logic.

### Change the contract later

1. Edit the manifest, checking [manifest authoring](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html) for type and compatibility guidance.
2. Re-run `go-sdk-generator generate` with the same input, output, and Go version.
3. Review the file diff before accepting it. Generation preserves stateful files by default; `--overwrite` also regenerates them, including files such as `go.mod`. Use it only when you intend to replace and review that state.
4. Run `go mod tidy`, `go generate ./...`, and the project's tests again in each affected Go module. Keep handwritten operation logic and project-specific wiring when resolving changes.

This repository generates parts of itself from [`generate.yml`](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generate.yml). Its [development guide](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md#code-generation) covers the repository-specific workflow. For CLI configuration, logging, and the full generated interface, consult [`DOCUMENTATION.md`](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DOCUMENTATION.md).


## Install and inspect go-sdk-generator

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


### When to use this guide

Start here before writing a manifest or running the generator. The CLI is named `go-sdk-generator`; its package is also named `go-sdk-generator`.

### Install on Linux

Once the appropriate package repository is configured, use the native package manager:

| System | Install commands |
| --- | --- |
| Debian or Ubuntu | `sudo apt update` then `sudo apt install go-sdk-generator` |
| Fedora or RHEL with dnf | `sudo dnf install go-sdk-generator` |
| RHEL or CentOS with yum | `sudo yum install go-sdk-generator` |

Released Linux packages include agent skills under `/etc/go-sdk-generator/.agents/skills`. For package upgrades, use your package manager's upgrade command. See the [installation skill](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/.agents/skills/install-go-sdk-generator/SKILL.md) for platform-specific troubleshooting.

### Run an OCI image

For container-based use, choose a published version and image variant:

```sh
docker run --rm ghcr.io/arm-software/go-sdk-generator:v<version>-alpine --help
```

To generate into the current directory, mount it and set the working directory so input and output paths refer to the mounted files:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/work" -w /work \
  ghcr.io/arm-software/go-sdk-generator:v<version>-alpine \
  generate -i generate.yml -o /work --go-version 1.27.3
```

Replace `<version>` with a published version and `1.27.3` with your target project's Go version.

#### Accessing GHCR

If the image is not publicly accessible to your account, authenticate with GHCR first. With the GitHub CLI already authenticated:

```sh
gh auth token | docker login ghcr.io -u "$(gh api user --jq .login)" --password-stdin
```

If `docker pull` or `docker run` returns `403 Forbidden`, check that your account or CI token has package-read access. Local GitHub CLI credentials may need the `read:packages` scope; refresh them, then log in again:

```sh
docker logout ghcr.io
gh auth refresh --scopes read:packages
gh auth token | docker login ghcr.io -u "$(gh api user --jq .login)" --password-stdin
```

See [GitHub's container registry documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry) for permissions and authentication details.

### Check the installation and contract

```sh
go-sdk-generator --version
go-sdk-generator --help
go-sdk-generator generate --help
go-sdk-generator schema
```

`schema` prints the embedded manifest schema as JSON, suitable for inspecting allowed fields with other tools. The [schema source](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml) is also available in the repository. To install the embedded skills into the current repository, run `go-sdk-generator agent --init`.


## Secret management in generated CLI tools

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


Use this guide when a [manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html) defines CLI configuration containing tokens, passwords or other secret strings. The generator can provide a separate `credentials` command for storing those values in the system keyring where supported.

### Mark secret inputs in the manifest

Set `secret: true` on a string-compatible CLI configuration field. For example, within a command's `configuration` list:

```yaml
- name: Token
  lang_type: string
  mapstructure_tag: token
  description: Token used by the command.
  secret: true
```

For a structured configuration value, you can instead mark an individual `bindings` entry as secret. The generator validates the type: a secret field or binding must resolve to a string-compatible value. Consult the [manifest schema](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml) for both `secret` fields and the [manifest-authoring skill](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/.agents/skills/manifest-authoring/SKILL.md) for authoring guidance.

### Store and load credentials

If the CLI has secret-marked inputs but no `Credentials` command, the generator creates one from those inputs. If a `Credentials` command already exists, it merges the secret-marked inputs into that command. The generated command stores its configuration in the system keyring instead of invoking SDK operation logic, and no GitHub Action wrapper is generated for it.

In the **generated tool**, inspect `<generated-binary> credentials --help` for its inputs. Run the command with the required values to store them when the platform supports a system keyring. An unsupported keyring reports an error rather than silently storing the values elsewhere. `go-sdk-generator` itself has no `credentials` command unless its own manifest defines secret inputs.

Commands configured to load from the keyring use non-empty stored values ahead of CLI flags, environment variables, configuration files and defaults. Such commands expose `--no-keyring` to disable keyring loading for that invocation. The [generated command reference](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DOCUMENTATION.md#cli-tool) describes configuration precedence; check the generated project's own command documentation for which commands enable keyring loading. A command cannot be configured to store to and load from the keyring at the same time.

### Security boundaries

- Keep actual secret values out of manifests, `default_value`, committed `.env` files and generated source: secret marking describes how an input is handled, but does not remove a literal value supplied in the contract.
- Prefer the system keyring for local credential storage where supported. For CI, supply credentials through the CI system's secret mechanism; see [GitHub Actions integration](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/use-github-actions.html).
- Generated `secretutil.ProtectedString` is currently a Go `string` alias. It does not itself encrypt values in memory or prevent a caller from logging them; handle values in handwritten operation code accordingly.


## Types, formats and default values

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


Use this reference when choosing `lang_type`, value shapes and `default_value` in a [generator manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html). The [schema](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml) defines the contract; this page explains what the built-in types produce.

### Built-in types and formats

The generator accepts native Go types and convenience aliases in `lang_type`.

| `lang_type` | Generated Go type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` | `string` | Plain string values. |
| `bool` | `bool` | Boolean values. |
| `int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64` | Same as input | Signed integers. |
| `uint`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64` | Same as input | Unsigned integers. |
| `float32`, `float64` | Same as input | Floating-point values. |
| `[]string` | `[]string` | String list values. |
| `[]byte` | `[]byte` | Byte slice values. |
| `any` | `any` | Arbitrary values. |
| `time.Duration`, `duration` | `time.Duration` | Durations such as `5m` or `5*time.Minute`. |
| `decimal` | `float64` | Convenience alias for decimal numbers. |
| `datetime` | `string` | RFC3339-style date/time input with special default handling. |
| `uuid` | `string` | UUID-formatted string. |
| `json`, `validJSON` | `string` | JSON payload stored as a string; `validJSON` enables strict JSON validation. |
| `url`, `uri`, `host`, `pathParameter` | `string` | URL-like strings; `uri` and `pathParameter` use specialised validators. |
| `connection`, `onlineTarget`, `service`, `server` | `httpUtils.RequestConfiguration` | HTTP request target configuration. |
| `protectedConnection`, `protectedService`, `protectedServer`, `behindAuthConnection`, `behindAuthService`, `behindAuthServer`, `serviceBehindAuth`, `serverBehindAuth` | `httpUtils.RequestConfiguration` | Request target configuration with authorisation-oriented defaults. |
| `email` | `string` | Email address string. |
| `ip` | `string` | IP address string. |
| `version`, `semver` | `string` | Semantic version strings. |
| `port` | `uint32` | Network port number. |
| `filepath`, `existingFilepath` | `string` | Filesystem paths; `existingFilepath` also requires the path to exist. |
| `hex` | `[]byte` | Hex-encoded bytes decoded at runtime. |
| `base64`, `byte`, `binary`, `regex` | `string` | Validated string-based formats. |

Declare project-specific types with `specification.additional_types`. For a pointer, list or iterator, prefer the manifest's `reference`, `list` and `iterator` flags to embedding Go syntax in `lang_type`. `list` and `iterator` cannot be combined. A final method argument marked `list: true` becomes variadic (`...T`). Use `enum` for closed string-like choices.

### Built-in `default_value` shortcuts

Most values are emitted as literals. The following shortcuts produce computed defaults; use them only when their behaviour suits the contract.

| Type | `default_value` | Generated behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `string` and string-like aliases such as `uuid`, `host`, `url`, `uri`, `email`, `ip`, `version`, `semver`, `base64`, `byte`, `binary`, `regex` | Any other value | Emit a quoted string literal. |
| String-like aliases | `hostname` | Use `os.Hostname()`. |
| String-like aliases | `uuid` | Generate a UUID with `idgen.GenerateUUID4()`. |
| String-like aliases | `temp`, `tempdir`, `temporary` | Use `filesystem.TempDirectory()`. |
| String-like aliases | `bin`, `bindir` | Use `xdg.BinHome`. |
| String-like aliases | `cache`, `cachedir` | Use `xdg.CacheHome`. |
| String-like aliases | `config`, `configdir`, `conf`, `configuration` | Use `xdg.ConfigHome`. |
| String-like aliases | `here` | Use the working directory from `filesystem.CurrentDirectory()`. |
| String-like aliases | `home` | Use `os.UserHomeDir()`. |
| String-like aliases | `<username>'s home` | Use `platform.GetHomeDirectory("<username>")`, for example `maddie's home`. |
| String-like aliases | `random` | Use `rand.Text()`. |
| String-like aliases | `now` | Use `time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)`. |
| String-like aliases | `func()...` | Emit the custom function default as-is. |
| `datetime` | `now` | Use `time.Now().UTC()`. |
| `datetime` | RFC3339 timestamp | Parse with `time.Parse(time.RFC3339, ...)`. |
| `duration` | `5m`, `1h30m`, etc. | Parse with `time.ParseDuration(...)`. |
| `duration` | Expression containing `time.` | Emit as-is, for example `5 * time.Minute`. |
| `connection`, `onlineTarget`, `service`, `server` | URL such as `https://some-mcp.org/mcp` | Build a default `httpUtils.RequestConfiguration`, set `Host` and use a generated user agent. |
| Protected and `behindAuth` connection/service/server aliases | URL such as `https://some-mcp.org/mcp` | Build an authorised `httpUtils.RequestConfiguration`, set the bearer scheme and `Host`, and use a generated user agent. |
| `hex` | Hex text such as `aaffbb77` | Decode with `hex.DecodeString(...)`. |
| `[]byte` | Any string | Emit as `[]byte("...")`. |
| `json` | JSON object text such as `{"key":1}` | Emit a quoted JSON string. |
| Numeric and boolean types | Literal such as `42`, `3.14`, `false` | Emit the corresponding Go literal. |


## Run the generator in GitHub Actions

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


Choose what the workflow step should do, then choose whether to use a published release or build an unreleased revision. Both actions verify the tool with `--version` before using it.

### Choose an action

| Action | Operating mode |
| --- | --- |
| `actions/generate` | Install the tool and run `go-sdk-generator generate` with structured inputs. |
| `actions/install-tool` | Install only; return a `cmd` output for later commands, loops or scripts. |

`workdir` determines where `generate` runs and how its relative paths are resolved. For install-only use, call the installed tool through the `cmd` output in subsequent steps.

### Choose a version mode

The action's `@ref` selects one of these modes. `action-ref` overrides that ref; `action-repo` selects a different repository, and `github-token` supplies access when the default workflow token is insufficient.

| Mode | Choose | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Published release** | An exact tag such as `@v0.47.0`, a major/minor ref such as `@v0` or `@v0.47`, or `@latest`. | Install the matching release. Major/minor refs select the latest matching stable release. |
| **Unreleased source** | A branch such as `@main` or a commit SHA. | Build and install the CLI from that revision, whether or not a release exists. |

With no ref (for example, a local action path without `action-ref`), the action tries the latest release. Using `./actions/generate` or `./actions/install-tool` does **not** by itself select a source build; set `action-ref` to a branch or SHA for that mode.

**Failure behaviour:** A release ref that cannot be resolved or installed fails the action; it neither skips execution nor switches to a source build. An unavailable branch/SHA or unsuccessful source build likewise fails. Check the ref and, if needed, the `github-token` permissions.

The [shared installer](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/actions/_shared/install-and-run.sh) and [action metadata](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/actions/generate/action.yml) define the exact ref resolution and inputs.

### Generate from a manifest

The manifest must exist in the checked-out workspace. This example installs a released binary and runs `generate`:

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Generate Go project
    uses: ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/actions/generate@v0
    with:
      input: generate.yml
      output: .
      go-version: '1.27.3'
```

To build the tool from the current `main` branch instead of installing a release, replace `@v0` with `@main`.

Set `go-version` to the **generated project's** target Go version, not the version used to build the action. The action defaults to `summary=github`, `logger=rich` and `annotation=github`; `go-version` corresponds to the CLI flag `--go-version` (or `-g`).

### Install for later steps

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Install generator
    id: generator
    uses: ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/actions/install-tool@v0
  - name: Inspect schema
    shell: bash
    run: '"${{ steps.generator.outputs.cmd }}" schema'
```

Use the install-only mode when later steps need custom shell processing. For container-based use, see [install and inspect](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/install-and-inspect.html). For agent-specific instructions, see the [GitHub Action integration skill](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/.agents/skills/using-go-sdk-generator-in-a-github-action/SKILL.md).


## What the generator produces

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


The [manifest](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/write-a-manifest.html) defines one concern and the user-facing operations around it. Depending on that contract, `go-sdk-generator` can create:

- a Go module layout for the SDK, with exported configuration and domain types;
- interfaces and implementation scaffolding for SDK operations;
- an optional [Cobra](https://cobra.dev/)-style CLI backed by the same configuration model and [Viper](https://github.com/spf13/viper)-style configuration sources;
- a reusable Go-based entrypoint for step-level [GitHub Actions](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/use-github-actions.html);
- generated documentation, release configuration in `pyproject.toml`, and supporting project files.

The [types and defaults reference](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/types-and-defaults.html) describes built-in value formats. The [generated command reference](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/DOCUMENTATION.md) covers this repository's Go SDK and CLI interfaces.

### What you still implement

Generation provides structure and boilerplate, not the domain-specific logic behind each operation. Implement the generated stubs in Go, then [regenerate and review the project](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/generate-a-project.html) when its contract changes.

### One operation, several ways to use it

- Import the generated SDK in another Go project and call its methods directly.
- Run the generated CLI locally, in scripts or in a container.
- Use a generated action in CI to invoke the same Go tool rather than duplicating its logic in shell or JavaScript.

The same implementation can serve library users, command-line users and automation while remaining testable as Go code. A generated action represents an operation or a step; a [GitHub Actions workflow](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows) or task runner still defines how multiple steps fit together. See [use GitHub Actions](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/use-github-actions.html) for workflow examples.

For GitHub-hosted repositories, those supporting files include repository workflows such as CI, release automation, dependency updates, and optional copyright-header maintenance when `specification.update_copyright_headers` is enabled.

As the generator gains improvements to documentation, support files, defaults and repository conventions, regenerated projects can adopt them. Review regenerated files, preserve handwritten implementation logic and [manage incompatible contract changes](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/evolving-a-contract.html) deliberately.


## Write a generator manifest

<!--
Copyright (C) 2026-2026 Arm Limited or its affiliates and Contributors. All rights reserved.
SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
-->


### When to use this guide

Write a YAML or JSON manifest to define one coherent set of user-facing Go operations. The manifest controls the generated SDK surface, optional CLI, configuration, documentation, and supporting files. Domain-specific operation logic is implemented afterwards in Go.

### Start from the contract

Use [`generator/schema/schema.yml`](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generator/schema/schema.yml) for the complete field definitions, or print the schema as JSON with `go-sdk-generator schema`. The repository's [`generate.yml`](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generate.yml) shows a real input. The key sections under `specification` are:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `package_name`, `main_module`, `name`, `description` | Project and SDK identity. |
| `repository_url`, `public` | Repository location and whether the project is public; used across generated project metadata and hosting integrations. |
| `interface` | Public Go operations and their arguments and results. |
| `global_configuration` | Values shared across the SDK and CLI. |
| `command_line_commands` | Optional binary and commands exposing those operations. |
| `additional_types` | Optional domain types used by the contract. |
| `tag_latest`, `update_copyright_headers` | Optional release tagging and copyright-header maintenance settings. |

When operations accept functional options, use `specification.options`; see [configure functional options](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/configure-options.html) for option wrappers, `value_field` and CLI bindings.

A minimal starting shape is:

```yaml
specification:
  package_name: example-tool
  main_module: example
  name: Example
  description: Verify an example project.
  licence: Apache-2.0
  interface:
    notCloseable: true
    namespace: github.com/example/
    methods:
      - name: Verify
        description: Verify an example project.
        returns:
          - name: err
            lang_type: error
            description: Verification failure, if any.
  global_configuration: []
```

This describes a library surface. Add `command_line_commands` if users also need a CLI; see the [repository manifest](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/generate.yml) for commands, flags, and shared configuration. Adapt the namespace, name, operation, and licence to your project. [What the generator produces](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/what-it-generates.html) explains the resulting project structure.

Repository-level automation can also be controlled from the top level of `specification`:

- `tag_latest` defaults to `false`. Set it to `true` to keep a `latest` tag pointing to the most recent stable release. Consumers can follow published releases without updating their references or tracking a development branch. Because the tag moves, builds that use it are not reproducible and can pick up breaking changes; pin a version when that matters. See [Docker's guidance on tags and aliases](https://github.com/docker-library/official-images#tags-and-aliases) and [pinning image versions](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/#pin-base-image-versions), and [GitHub's guidance on managing action versions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/create-and-publish-actions/manage-custom-actions).
- `update_copyright_headers` defaults to `true`. Copyright headers identify the copyright holders and ownership of source files, often with applicable years and an SPDX licence identifier. They support attribution, clear licensing terms, and automated licence checks. For GitHub-hosted projects, enabling this setting generates a workflow that updates headers on pull requests and proposes a maintenance pull request on scheduled or manual runs. Generator upgrades refresh headers too. Set it to `false` to opt out. See the [REUSE specification](https://reuse.software/spec-3.3/) and [GNU copyright notice guidance](https://www.gnu.org/prep/maintain/html_node/Copyright-Notices.html).

### Model values deliberately

- Use specific `lang_type` aliases such as `duration`, `uuid`, `filepath`, or `service` where they match the value. See [types, formats and defaults](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/types-and-defaults.html) for the complete built-in reference. Prefer `reference: true`, `list: true`, or `iterator: true` to encoding shapes into the type string; `list` and `iterator` cannot be combined.
- Use `enum` for closed string choices, `constraints` for validation and relationships, and `example` or `examples` for representative values. These feed generated validation, help, documentation, and action inputs.
- Keep truly shared values in `global_configuration`; put operation-specific values on that command. Mark credentials with `secret: true` and follow [secret management in generated CLI tools](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/secret-management.html) for storage and loading behaviour.
- Give operations verb names and write descriptions from a user's perspective. Avoid defining a transport endpoint as an entire operation if the intended action is a higher-level workflow.
- For incompatible changes to a published contract, document a replacement with `deprecation_notice` before removing the old surface. Follow [breaking changes and deprecation](https://ARM-software.github.io/go-sdk-generator/guides/evolving-a-contract.html).

The [manifest-authoring skill](https://github.com/ARM-software/go-sdk-generator/blob/main/.agents/skills/manifest-authoring/SKILL.md) contains a detailed checklist for agents and maintainers.
